question: What can public sources establish about Acha Reef locality, sanctuary status, and conflicting 500-hectare versus 6-hectare area statements?
purpose: Resolve source provenance before spatial or species projection. This is not a current legal-status determination, fish survey, or geometry validation.
searchMethod: Reviewed the June 2000 Coastal Resources Center/PCAMRD report, the 2022 open-access Ragay Gulf study, the official 2004-2030 CALABARZON plan, an indexed official Tagkawayan LGU notice dated 13 April 2026, an indexed third-party Scribd CLWUP preview, and the accessible 13-page front matter/contents copy of the 2002 PhilReefs atlas. The official LGU page returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch; the Scribd document was not authenticated. This is a bounded source-provenance review.

findings.historicalLocality: The June 2000 report Table II row 74 lists Acha Reef, Region 4, Quezon, Tagkawayan, Candalapdap. The report says this preliminary compilation is incomplete and not ground-truthed; listed sites may not meet its sanctuary definition. Acha's establishment-year field is blank.
findings.crossTownLocality: The 2022 Ragay Gulf article describes Acha Reef between Guinayangan and Tagkawayan and names it among reef areas where interviewees fished for slipper lobster. Its 2017-2018 purposive interviews are not a finfish survey or a mapped boundary.
findings.areaConflict: The official 2004-2030 regional plan reports 500 hectares. An unauthenticated third-party Scribd preview attributed to a 2021-2030 Tagkawayan CLWUP reports 6 hectares and a position 2.7 km south of Sibalon Island. Neither value is accepted as geometry or reconciled by averaging.
findings.planApprovalContext: An official Tagkawayan LGU post dated 13 April 2026 says Quezon PLUC endorsed the CLWUP on 7 April before Sangguniang Bayan and Sangguniang Panlalawigan final approval. This is the status reported on that date, not proof of whether later approvals occurred; the post does not discuss Acha Reef.
findings.speciesAndLegalLimits: The 2000 directory and 2022 interview study do not provide Acha-specific finfish taxonomy. The 2000 report is not a legal instrument; the atlas chapter is unavailable; and the 2003 WWF aggregate is not allocated to Acha. Current sanctuary designation, boundary, species, and fishing rules remain unverified.

accessAndRights.crc: Full 2000 report reviewed; no item-specific open license identified. Use short factual citations only.
accessAndRights.lgu: Official LGU search-indexed notice reviewed; direct page fetch returned HTTP 403.
accessAndRights.thirdPartyClwup: Preview text only; uploader and rights unknown; no final official copy or signed approval verified. Do not reproduce or operationalize its 6-hectare claim.
accessAndRights.regionalPlan: Official regional PDF reviewed; no item-specific open reuse terms identified.
accessAndRights.slipperLobsterStudy: Open-access 2022 journal PDF reviewed; locality context is for slipper-lobster interviews, not finfish presence.
accessAndRights.atlas: All rights reserved; accessible PDF copy lacks the Acha chapter.
accessAndRights.rawRetention: No source PDFs or plan pages were added to the repository.

decision.reason: Locality is supported by historical source statements, but the 2000 list is explicitly unground-truthed and the 6-hectare CLWUP preview is unauthenticated; the 500-hectare value is historical and unmapped.

nextAction: Retrieve the final approved Tagkawayan CLWUP with maps and technical notes, plus an official current sanctuary instrument/boundary. Seek authorized access to the Acha atlas chapter or an independent dated, station-resolved, rights-cleared finfish survey. Keep both area statements out of geometry.

sources.supports: 2000 preliminary site-list row 74 and its ground-truthing/legal-status caveats.
Official LGU plan-status statement published 13 April 2026.
Unverified third-party preview text with a conflicting 6-hectare Acha statement; retrieval lead only.
Historical official plan places Acha in Tagkawayan and reports 500 hectares.
2022 study-area description places Acha between Guinayangan and Tagkawayan; survey is slipper-lobster interview context.
